records.headline: Binance freezes billions after suspected $6.3 billion security breach
records.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer allowed hackers to steal an estimated $6.3 billion. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $1.57 billion and $800 million respectively in linked assets. Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low, and Coinbase Global shares fell 4.8%, but analysts said the market appeared confident Binance had enough financial resources to cover user losses.

candidate.concept: Binance hack: compromised laptop enabled estimated $6.3B theft; stablecoins frozen; markets dipped but analyst confidence held

objects.description: Open laptop 160 units wide drawn around origin, screen angled back, keyboard base below
Warning triangle with exclamation, about 80 units tall
Money bag shape about 130 units tall representing stolen funds, drawn around origin
Padlock about 140 units tall representing frozen assets
Gold coin with T letter for Tether, 90 units diameter
Muted coin with C arc for Circle, 90 units diameter
Vertical bar chart column that shrinks to show market drop, 140 units tall at full size
Shield with checkmark about 150 units tall for analyst confidence

shots.action: Laptop sits left with alert badge popping on; money bag travels from laptop all the way across canvas to far right representing stolen funds
Tether coin slides in from far left and Circle coin slides in from far right; both move to center flanking lock; lock slams down over both coins
Bar on left shrinks tall to short showing market dip; shield on right starts mid-size and grows fully showing analyst confidence

issues: Shot 1 – money-bag (moneybag) does not travel across the canvas as planned: in the middle frame it is still overlapping the laptop area, and by the final frame it has jumped to the far right but there is no visible mid-journey position showing continuous travel; the motion reads as a cut/jump rather than a traversal, so the 'stolen funds crossing the canvas' action is not legibly shown.

Shot 1 – the alert badge fades almost to invisible (o=0.3) by the final frame, so the setup object that signals 'compromise' disappears at the result stage, leaving the laptop without its warning indicator just when the theft is complete; this undermines readability.

Shot 2 – the lock is already centred and large in the first (t=0) frame, so there is no visible drop action from top to coins; the 'lock slams down' motion is not perceptible across the three sampled columns shown on the contact sheet.

Shot 2 – Circle coin icon is a faint, barely distinguishable grey circle with a 'C'-like mark at phone size; it is not clearly recognisable as distinct from a generic coin, making the two-coin narrative hard to read.

Shot 3 – the bar labelled 'Bitcoin −more than 3%, Coinbase −4.8%' represents two separate assets (Bitcoin price and Coinbase shares) with a single bar, implying a shared or equal magnitude drop and conflating two distinct data points into one visual object; this is misleading and unsupported by the source which gives different percentages for each.

Shot 3 – the shield is already present and nearly full-size in the t=0 (setup) frame, so the 'grows from mid-size to full' animation is not visible in the contact sheet columns; there is minimal perceptible size change between the middle and final frames.
Shot 3 – the bar shrinks to a very short, wide rectangle that at phone size could be misread as a baseline or axis line rather than a reduced bar, reducing clarity of the 'market dip' metaphor.

Shot 1 label 'est. $6.3B stolen' is correctly qualified, but the visual shows a generic money-bag with no denomination indicator, so viewers cannot distinguish this figure from any other amount; a '$6.3B' text overlay or distinct sizing cue on the bag is absent.

Shot 1: The coin does not visibly travel across the canvas between t0, t0.45, and t0.9 — it appears in roughly the same right-side position in all three frames with no meaningful positional movement, so the 'launches and travels far right' action is not shown. This is effectively a static icon, not an animation of theft.; Shot 2: The two coins do not slide in from opposite sides; they appear already present at t0 flanking a lock that is already rendered. No visible motion of coins moving inward is shown across frames — the lock and coins appear nearly identical in all three frames, making the 'slide in and lock slams down' action invisible.; Shot 3: The shield grows from an invisible seed (tiny dot, essentially invisible at phone size) to full size, but the seed object at t0 and t0.45 is so small as to be imperceptible — it appears as a faint dot that is not recognisable as any object. This fails the 'objects recognisable at phone size' requirement.; Shot 3: The down arrow does not visibly change position or size across the three frames — it is static in all three columns, showing no falling motion. The stated action 'down arrow falls from top' is not illustrated by any visible movement between frames.; Shot 1: The alert badge appears already present in both t0.45 and t0.9 with no visible difference between those two frames, providing no meaningful progression in the second half of the animation.; Shot 2: The two coins representing Tether and Circle are visually identical and unlabelled by distinct iconography (both show the same generic coin symbol), making it impossible to distinguish Tether from Circle visually without relying solely on text labels placed far from the objects.; Shot 3: The shield icon at full size (t0.9) is acceptable, but because the growth from seed is imperceptible, the conceptual contrast between 'market dip' and 'analyst confidence' growing is lost — the two sides of the shot do not show a meaningful visual counterpoint across frames.

Shot 1 – money-bag/stolen-funds object never travels across the canvas as planned. At t0 there is no money bag at all; at t0.45 a coin-like badge appears overlapping the laptop but stays there; at t0.9 it has faded/shrunk rather than reaching the far right. The core action (funds traveling from laptop to far right) is absent and the $6.3B stolen label has no distinct moving object representing it at phone size.; Shot 1 – the 'est. $6.3B stolen' label sits far right in every frame with no corresponding visible object there, making the label appear to float over empty space in t0 and t0.9, which is illegible and unsupported visually.; Shot 2 – the lock does not slam DOWN over the coins as planned. In the final frame (t0.9) the lock is positioned between/behind the coins rather than covering them, and the shackle is open, failing to show the 'frozen' state clearly. The lock closing action is not visible.; Shot 2 – the Circle coin icon (showing a backwards/mirrored C) is barely distinguishable from a generic coin at phone size and could be confused with another symbol; it does not clearly read as the Circle (USDC) brand icon.; Shot 3 – the bar (Bitcoin dip) shrinks from tall to short correctly, but the shield (analyst confidence) is nearly the same small size in t0, t0.45, and only marginally larger in t0.9. The growth is too subtle to read as meaningful 'growing fully' at phone size; the motion does not clearly convey increasing confidence.; Shot 3 – a single bar is used to represent both 'Bitcoin −more than 3%' and 'Coinbase −4.8%' drops, but only one bar is shown. Two separate bars are implied by the label; showing one bar risks implying a single unsourced combined quantity rather than two distinct cited figures.; Shot 3 – the shield checkmark is present and essentially static across all three frames (same icon, same check, negligible size change), meaning the 'analysts: confident' element shows no meaningful visible transformation to justify its presence as an animated element versus a static label.; Shot 1 – at t0.9 the alert badge fades to near-invisible (very light/dotted appearance), making the frame effectively show only a plain laptop with no action indicator, leaving the result frame without a clear depiction of the completed theft action.

records.headline: Hong Kong leader apologises for government failures in residential fire that killed 168 people
records.text: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee apologised for government failures that contributed to a November 2025 fire at Wang Fuk Court housing complex that killed 168 people. An independent investigation found decades of regulatory failure and "lax enforcement" by four government departments. Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned, and authorities charged seven individuals and two companies with offences including manslaughter, though some victims' families said political accountability fell short.

candidate.concept: Hong Kong housing fire: apology, regulatory failure, and resignation

objects.description: Tall residential housing block with window grid
Stylized fire flame rising upward
Static clock face with tick marks
Long clock minute hand rotates around center
Short clock hour hand rotates around center
Investigation report document
Static door frame with hinge side on left
Door panel hinged at left edge, swings open/closed by rotating around left edge
Legal gavel head with handle for criminal charges

shots.action: Flame erupts and surges up the full height of the tower
Clock hands spin many full rotations conveying decades of failure while report document slides in from right
Door swings shut from fully open to closed on left hinge representing Ho's resignation
Gavel swings down in a clear arc and strikes the surface representing charges filed against individuals and companies

issues: Shot 2 – Clock hands: Across all three frames the clock shows the same hand position (roughly 12 o'clock, vertical). No visible rotation occurs between t0, t0.45 and t0.9. The plan calls for many full rotations conveying decades of failure; the rendered frames show a static clock, making the motion meaningless.

Shot 2 – Report document: The report/document icon appears already present in the same position in all three frames with no visible slide-in from the right. The planned left-ward translation is not visible in the rendered contact sheet.

Shot 3 – Door action shared with gavel (same shot row): Shot 3 uses the label '9 charged (7+2)' which belongs to the gavel shot (Shot 4), while Shot 4 also uses '9 charged (7+2)'. The door shot (resignation of Ho) should carry 'Ho resigned' as its primary label on both objects; the gavel label appearing on the door shot conflates two separate actions and misleads the viewer.

Shot 4 – Gavel: The gavel appears already close to its struck position in all three frames; the arc swing from raised (-65°) to struck (+18°) is not clearly distinguishable across the three sampled columns, making the motion ambiguous at contact-sheet review size.

Shot 3 – Door motion: Between t0 and t0.45 the door appears nearly fully closed already (large purple panel visible), with little perceptible change to t0.9. The scale-based swing from sx=0.08 to sx=1 is not clearly readable as a hinged door closing; it looks like the door panel simply appears/grows rather than swinging on a hinge, which does not clearly represent 'Ho resigned'.

Shot 1 – Flame position at t0: The small flame starts at the base but is barely distinguishable from a decorative element at phone size; however the growth to full tower height by the final frame is the clearest motion in the sheet and is acceptable. Minor issue only.

Label '9 charged (7+2)' appears on Shot 3 (door row) instead of or in addition to Shot 4 (gavel row), duplicating across two distinct shots and failing to pair each shot with its own unique label set as required.

Shot 2 clock failure: the plan calls for clock hands spinning many full rotations to convey 'decades', but across t0/t45/t90 the clock hands move only slightly (roughly a quarter-turn total). This is not a meaningful visible rotation conveying decades of elapsed time; it reads as a nearly static clock icon.; Shot 2 wrong motion type: the entire clock body does not rotate (which would itself be wrong per the brief), nor do the hands spin convincingly. The subtle hand shift does not communicate 'decades of regulatory failure' and violates the requirement that successive frames show meaningful visible movement.; Shot 3 door failure: the plan specifies a door swinging shut from open to closed on a left hinge (hinged door). What is rendered across all three frames is a rectangular door frame with a flat panel — the door does not visibly open or close between frames; it appears essentially the same (closed/flat) in t0, t45, and t90. There is no visible swing motion to represent resignation/departure.; Shot 3 gavel motion is minimal and ambiguous: the gavel icon shifts slightly in angle between frames but does not show a clear downward strike progression. At phone size this reads as a static or decorative icon rather than a gavel striking.; Shot 1 label placement: 'government failures' and '168 killed' labels are repeated identically across all three time-steps with no progression, so the label does not 'progress from setup to result' as the plan states — the label content never changes to reflect the result state.; Shot 3 combines two distinct actions (door closing for resignation AND gavel striking for charges) in a single shot without clear temporal separation, making it ambiguous which action is occurring at each frame and violating the one-clear-action-per-shot requirement.; '7 charged' label omits the two companies also charged per the source ('seven individuals and two companies'), which could mislead about the scope of charges; the label should reflect both individuals and entities or use a qualifier.
Label invents quantity 9

records.headline: China expels record 33 members from Communist Party amid intensified purges under Xi
records.text: China expelled a record 33 members from the Communist Party at its fifth plenum this week, amid intensified purges under Xi Jinping. Only 279 of 376 Central Committee members originally named in 2022 attended the gathering, the highest number of absences in modern Chinese history. Xi has removed so many high-ranking officials—51 in his current term alone—that observers worry there are few suitable candidates to fill vacancies ahead of the party congress expected in late 2027.

candidate.concept: Record party purges under Xi Jinping leave the Central Committee depleted and future leadership in question

objects.description: Tall rectangle representing the full 376-member Central Committee, used as landing surface for stamp
Heavy rectangular rubber-stamp block with ink pad base and EXPELLED banner, drops and squashes on impact
Accent-filled bar representing 279 attending members, proportion of full bar height
Muted cap block representing 97 absent members sitting atop the attend fill
Outline rectangle spanning full 376-member bar height, no fill
Static institutional doorway frame with lintel
Door panel hinged at its left edge (x=-50 local) swings from open to closed
Bold question mark with dot representing unfilled leadership vacancies

shots.action: Stamp block falls from above onto the member bar, squashes flat on impact, then rebounds to upright, branding expulsion
Attend fill rises from bottom of bar outline to 74% height while absent cap slides down from above to rest on top, showing the 279-vs-97 split
Door leaf swings fully shut on left hinge while vacancy question mark rises into view on right, showing removed officials leave unfillable vacancies

issues: Shot 1 – stamp squash-and-rebound is not visible: across all three columns the stamp appears to have already landed and sits statically on top of the bar with no discernible change in shape or position between frames; the key animation (falling, squashing flat, rebounding) is absent from the rendered contact sheet, making the action unclear.

Shot 1 – the 'member bar' object that should be branded/stamped shows no visible mark, ink impression, or branded text appearing on it at any frame, so the stated expulsion branding is not communicated.

Shot 3 – door leaf swing is not clearly shown: the door appears nearly closed or fully closed across all three columns with only a very slight difference in the gap visible; the wide-open-to-shut sweep required to communicate 'swings fully shut' is not visible at phone size.

Shot 3 – the label '51 removed this term' appears in every column of row 3 but the number 51 is not illustrated by any counted or enumerated visual element; combined with a static door icon this makes the shot carry an unsourced quantitative implication without any supporting visual, conflating two separate facts (51 removals and 'few candidates') into one ambiguous scene.

Shot 3 – vacancy question mark is visible in columns 2 and 3 but is very small (roughly icon-sized) and at phone scale will be illegible/unrecognisable, failing the phone-size recognisability requirement.

Shot 2 – the bar fill animation (attend_fill growing) does appear to progress across frames, which is positive, but in column 1 (t=0) the bar is already partially filled rather than starting near-empty as the plan specifies (sy≈0.01), suggesting the rendered start state does not match the plan and the reveal is truncated.

Shot 1 – stamp action not visible: t0 shows only a plain purple rectangle (the 'member bar'), t0.45 and t0.9 show a static stamp/seal icon already fully placed with no downward motion, squash deformation, or impact. The planned drop-and-squash animation is absent; frames are effectively static icons, not successive motion.; Shot 1 – the stamp icon (circle with X) does not read as a stamp branding expulsion at phone size; it resembles a 'no entry' or cancel symbol and is disconnected from the rectangle below rather than landing on it.; Shot 2 – wrong part moves: the bar grows from the left (attendees fill in), but the plan is to 'reveal the reported proportion'. More critically, at t0.45 the filled portion looks roughly 25% and at t0.9 roughly 60%, neither of which represents 279/376 (≈74%). The final frame does not reach the correct proportion, implying an unsourced attendance ratio.; Shot 2 – no visible separation between 'attended' and 'absent' segments in the final frame to make the 279-vs-97 split legible at phone size; a single growing bar without a clear absent-remainder section does not convey the absence story.; Shot 3 – door frame does not visibly hinge/swing: across all three frames the door leaf appears in the same nearly-closed position with no progressive rotation on a hinge axis. The plan requires the leaf to swing fully shut; the motion is imperceptible or absent.; Shot 3 – the question mark in t0 is partially clipped/cut off at the bottom of the canvas, making it illegible at phone size.; Shot 3 – the '51 removed this term' label persists unchanged across all three frames while the door shows no meaningful change, leaving no visual explanation of why 51 removals cause vacancies; the two elements (door and question mark) appear side by side with no causal connection shown.; Shot 1 – no squash/impact frame is distinguishable; all three frames lack meaningful visible movement, violating the requirement that successive frames show visible transformation rather than static or merely fading icons.
Label invents quantity 97
